items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: Basie offered me a job. And I said, why didn't you ever ask me before, for God's sake? And he said, "I couldn't afford to pay you." And I said, "you've offered me $100.00 a week more than Benny's playing me."

ctx.x: Yeah, very competent, very quick. He could sit down and dash things off. A lot of the arrangers in those days studied from Shillinger, who had the mathematics system, because they had to grind these arrangements out. So they'd write out a formula and it would be rhythms. But mostly they would sound like that, too. The sounds would come out pretty bad.

And Raymond Scott used to write -- I played with him for a while, too, on the Lucky Strike Program, and he would write an arrangement and he would say, 'come on, make it sound like Basie.' And I would say, 'you don't write like Basie.' He said, 'that doesn't make any difference, play it so it sounds' -- then he'd say, 'well, maybe we won't make this one sound like Basie, we'll make this one sound like Ellington.' And he got these simple little harmonies in there.
